Who we are:
•   Security Services is responsible for the protection of all City assets including people and infrastructure. Programs
    include infrastructure protective systems, security audits, fire safety, downtown camera management, incident and
    emergency response, guard services, event security planning and executive protection.
•   In addition, we are key partners in community safety through management of community protests and events,
    participation in the Informed Response Program and Community Safety Audits.
 What we do:
•   Corporate Security contributes towards a safe and secure environment for City staff and residents through a
    commitment to prevention, preparedness, and response. This includes the protection of staff, residents, and
    infrastructure assets.

Why we do it:
•   Essential – The provision of effective security services at municipal facilities and across our community contributes

 Environmental, Socio-economic Equity and Governance (ESG) Considerations
Environmental, Socio-economic Equity and Governance Profile for this service:

Environmental:
•   This business plan is expected to help reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the community. We recognize the
    importance of environmental sustainability and strive to minimize its ecological footprint. In all our operations, we
    consider the potential environmental impacts and initiative measures to mitigate them. This includes opting for eco-
    friendly vehicles in our fleet and implementing waste management strategies that prioritize recycling and reduction of
    waste. We also promote environmental awareness and education among our staff and the community.

Socio-economic Equity:
•   Security Services ensures equal access to employment opportunities within the Service regardless of an individual's
    socio-economic background. This approach fosters diversity and allows for a broader range of perspectives, skills,
    and experiences within the workforce, enhancing the effectiveness of the area.

Governance:
•   We strive to enhance public trust and confidence through clear communication, engagement with the community, and
    the establishment of strong partnerships with all partners. This is achieved by actively seeking feedback, addressing
    concerns or complaints, and continuously evaluating the Service's governance structure and processes. By prioritizing
    good governance, the City of London Security Services area can effectively fulfill its mandate and provide service in a
    responsible and accountable manner.
 The following section provides an overview of the key activities the service plans to undertake from 2024 to 2027 to
implement the Corporation’s 2023 to 2027 Strategic Plan, as well as an overview of the risks and challenges the service is
anticipated to experience during this period:

Service Highlights 2024 to 2027
•   With the assistance of Information Technology Services, develop and implement an internal service request portal
    which will improve efficiency, service delivery, and accountability.
•   Completion of the Downtown Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) Security Camera Program to provide coverage
    throughout the Core Area.
•   Relocation and expansion of the Security Operations Centre to support safety and security of the new Rapid Transit
    shelters throughout the City of London and the expansion of the Downtown Camera Program.
•   Security Services will continue to focus on asset protection and community safety including expanded efforts related to
    additional facilities as part of growing community.
•   Security Services will also continue to partner on the Informed Response Program and work with Business
    Improvement Areas to conduct security and safety audits with a focus of improving overall safety in the core area.
•   Work with key internal and external partners to support the City’s commitment to a “Safe London for Women, Girls,
    Gender-Diverse and Trans People”.

Risks and Challenges Anticipated in 2024 to 2027
•   Over the past few years there has been a significant increase in the number of public protests over various contentious
    issues. These protests have a potential to escalate quickly which create safety concerns for both participants and the
    public. We will continue to collaborate with our partners to ensure protests are conducted with a safety-first mindset.
•   There continues to be increased concern regarding the safety of our community both in general and in relation to City
    facilities and parks. Incident frequency continues to increase as the City grows. We will need to find innovative ways
    and partnerships to address these concerns.

Purpose
Sets guidelines for video surveillance to support public safety in compliance with privacy requirements. The policy safeguards privacy while protecting individuals and municipal assets.
Keywords
Video Surveillance, Public Safety, Property Protection, Privacy act
Purpose
This Video Surveillance Policy governs the Town’s use of video surveillance at properties owned and leased by the Town in strict accordance with the relevant provisions of Ontario’s
Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection Act (MFIPPA).
Policy Statement
The Town of Midland (the Town) recognizes the importance of balancing each individual’s right to privacy with the need to protect the safety and security of its employees, clients, visitors and property. The use of video surveillance systems is necessary for safety and security reasons, but such systems must be designed to minimize intrusion on privacy. Where this balance is appropriately struck, the use of video surveillance cameras is an effective means of ensuring that the Town’s facilities and properties are operating in a safe and secure manner.
Guided by a commitment to public safety, crime prevention and stewardship of publicly owned assets, the Town may, where warranted by law, use video surveillance systems in municipally owned buildings, or at municipally operated facilities, parks and open spaces.
